No. My previous message was wrong. The Great Wall is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon, and it isn't the only human-made structure claimed to be, since none are. From about 384,000 km, even continents appear as blurry features, and no individual human structure can be resolved.

The wall is also hard to see from low Earth orbit (~400 km). It is long but mostly under 10 meters wide, and its color blends with the surrounding terrain. Astronauts, including China's Yang Liwei in 2003, have reported being unable to pick it out unaided. Cities, airports, and greenhouse clusters are easier to spot from orbit, mainly at night or under favorable lighting.
